system.title: SpecGuard
system.value: Teams keep the intent behind their code as the source of truth, and can prove at any moment that the code still delivers it.

nodes.title: SpecGuard
nodes.value: Teams keep the intent behind their code as the source of truth, and can prove at any moment that the code still delivers it.

nodes.title: Agentic Verification
nodes.value: The running system is judged against what its specs say it is for, by a browser agent that can see and use it safely, so requirements are verified end to end and not only line by line.

claims.text: Validation targets specs that declare a `url:`, accepts a single spec, all specs or one app, resolves relative URLs against a base URL override, and skips with a message a spec that has no URL.

tests.title: scenario 3: spec without url is skipped

claims.text: For each spec the agent perceives the page through a screenshot and an accessibility snapshot, plans a short list of atomic browser actions from the acceptance criteria, performs them and then judges each criterion against the resulting state.

Every acceptance criterion receives exactly one verdict from PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED or INCONCLUSIVE, a FAIL cites its evidence, and a failed LLM call or unavailable evidence yields INCONCLUSIVE rather than a pass.

tests.title: scenario 2: FAIL verdict → exitCode 2
scenario 4: blocked action recorded in results

claims.text: The command exits with the validation-failed code (2) when any criterion or login fails and 0 otherwise, so skipped specs and blocked actions alone do not fail a run.

tests.title: scenario 1: all criteria pass → exitCode 0
scenario 2: FAIL verdict → exitCode 2

claims.text: Screenshots and page evidence are stored per spec under `.specguard/evidence/`, and every run appends an entry with its verdicts and overall result to `.specguard/validation-history.json`.

tests.title: scenario 3: saves screenshot and returns file path
validation history written to .specguard/validation-history.json

claims.text: An optional review step, skipped with `--no-review` or for specs with no UI sections, produces a typed issue report of functional, UX, accessibility and visual problems under `.specguard/reports/`.

Planned actions are classified as safe, destructive or outbound by deterministic whole-word keyword rules, with the real control's role and accessible name taking precedence over the planner's description when the target is known.

tests.title: scenario 1: destructive keywords
scenario 2: outbound keywords
scenario 3: safe actions return safe
scenario 4: case insensitive matching
empty string returns safe
does not match a keyword inside a longer word
matches inflections, camelCase and snake_case
keeps multi-word phrases together
filling a text field is safe whatever the description says
an activating control is judged by its own name
a control with no name falls back to the description
an unknown element falls back to word matching on the description

claims.text: Destructive and outbound actions are blocked before execution and surfaced as BLOCKED verdicts with the reason, deny and allow rules in configuration override the built-in lists, and outbound actions run only when explicitly allowed while destructive ones are never allowed.

tests.title: builds a BlockedAction for destructive classification
builds a BlockedAction for outbound classification
deny blocks as destructive, allow wins over the built-in lists
allowOutbound lets outbound through and never destructive
scenario 4: blocked action recorded in results

claims.text: Authentication profiles support form login, saved browser state, header and token credentials, and a project-supplied script, and a login succeeds when a configured success URL or selector is reached, or otherwise when the browser leaves the login page.

tests.title: logged in means off the login page, or on the configured success URL
succeeds when the browser leaves the login page, including a /login-success page
fails when the login page is still showing
without waitForURL it still refuses to report success on the login page
header: resolves each header from its env var and names the missing one
token: Authorization Bearer by default, configurable header and prefix
storageState: uses .specguard/auth/<profile>.json when it exists
token and header succeed when their env vars are set, and fail naming the variable
script: runs the project module, and rejects a path outside the project
storageState: an existing file is a ready session with no login
storageState: without a file it logs in with the form and saves the state under .specguard/auth
storageState: no file and no form configured is a clear error

claims.text: A login failure, unknown profile or missing credential environment variable is reported as a clear authentication failure for the affected specs, and a successful login is cached so each profile logs in once per run.

tests.title: scenario 1: successful login caches and returns success
scenario 2: missing password env var returns error without throwing
scenario 3: unknown profile returns error
failed login is not cached
removes cached sessions so authenticate runs again
a failed login closes its context, is not cached, and is retried
an unknown profile or missing credentials is an auth failure, not a throw

claims.text: Each auth profile runs in its own browser context and a spec without a profile runs in an anonymous context that is never logged in.

tests.title: gives each auth profile its own context, reuses it, and keeps anonymous pages on the first context
passes the profile context options (headers) when the context is created

claims.text: Credentials are read only from environment variables and never appear in config output, evidence, history, logs or LLM prompts, and error text derived from a login is redacted.

tests.title: redacts credentials from login failure error messages
scenario 4: replaces credential values with [REDACTED]
a failed form login redacts credentials from the error

claims.text: Page text, accessibility text and console errors pass through the redactor before reaching the LLM, and no screenshot is sent when images are disallowed in configuration.
The browser is headless unless configured or `--headed` is passed, runs locally or in Docker as configured, and a missing Playwright installation produces an error with install instructions.

tests.title: scenario 1: launches headless Chromium and returns a handle
scenario 2: throws PlaywrightUnavailableError when not installed

claims.text: Evidence, saved login state and report directories are created with a `.gitignore` that excludes their contents.
validation goals are built per capability from its Users & Journeys and Scenarios, so the agent walks real user journeys instead of isolated criteria.
the judge also receives the capability's Problem & Value and returns a capability-level judgement of whether the observed behaviour delivers the stated value, reporting gaps as findings.

tests.title: picks up a v2 capability with only a base URL, walks several rounds, and judges value [rounds-and-value]
fails the capability when the value is judged NO even if every requirement passes [value-no]

claims.text: verdicts are written into the proof ledger with evidence marked as agentic, so `check` treats browser verification as first-class proof alongside test results.

tests.title: records PASS and FAIL as agentic proof, matching claim ids exactly, never by substring [agentic-proof]
treats an empty verdict list as inconclusive, never as a pass, and records no proof [empty-verdicts]

claims.text: `verify` takes every v2 capability when given a base URL, even one with no `url:` of its own, and walks up to `validate.maxRounds` (default 3) plan-act rounds so one run can cross pages; the page is not reloaded between rounds

tests.title: picks up a v2 capability with only a base URL, walks several rounds, and judges value [rounds-and-value]
honours validate.maxRounds [max-rounds]
skips a capability when there is no URL to verify it from [needs-url]
lists as "already taken" only the actions that were actually performed [taken-only-performed]

claims.text: Only PASS and FAIL verdicts are written as proof; BLOCKED and INCONCLUSIVE never overwrite a proof a test run earned, and a verdict is matched to a requirement by its id (exact, or followed by a delimiter) or its exact text, never by substring

tests.title: records PASS and FAIL as agentic proof, matching claim ids exactly, never by substring [agentic-proof]
does not let BLOCKED or INCONCLUSIVE overwrite a proof a test run already earned [no-downgrade]

claims.text: A capability whose value is judged NO fails the verification even when every requirement passes, and the judgement with its gaps is written to `.specguard/reports/verify-<spec>.json`

tests.title: fails the capability when the value is judged NO even if every requirement passes [value-no]

claims.text: The planner may take `click`, `fill`, `navigate` (same site only), `waitFor` and `assertText` steps, a step that fails or does not hold is reported as `[action-failed]` instead of being swallowed, and `verify --emit-tests` (or `validate.emitTests`) turns a passing run in which every step ran into a `@playwright/test` file under `paths.e2eTests` (default `tests/e2e`) that starts from `BASE_URL`, carries `[layer: e2e]`, tags only the claims that have an assertion step of their own, is not written when a value would be redacted, and never replaces a file it did not generate

tests.title: replays every step, escapes values, and starts from BASE_URL when set
tags only the passing claims that have an assertion of their own
writes nothing for no steps, and refuses a step whose value the redactor would change
names the file after the capability
writes a Playwright test and tags only the requirements an assertion checks [emit-tagged]
writes nothing unless asked, by flag or validate.emitTests [emit-opt-in]
does not emit a test from a run in which a step failed, and says why, and reports the failed step [emit-incomplete]
refuses to navigate off the site under test [emit-same-site]
keeps a test file it did not generate, and refuses values the redactor would mask [emit-safe-writes]

claims.text: Page content the model reads (the title, the accessibility tree, the HTML, console errors) and imported or fetched documents are fenced as untrusted data (`<untrusted-...>` tags the content cannot close, a closing tag inside it is defanged), every system message says that nothing inside the fence is an instruction, and what the model proposes is still classified and guarded deterministically, never trusted because it asked

tests.title: wraps text in a labelled fence and says in the system message that the fence holds data
cannot be closed from the inside: a closing tag in the text is defanged, whatever its case
makes a safe tag name out of any label
fences the imported document as untrusted data, so a sentence inside it cannot close the fence or pass as an instruction
fences the page text and tree the model reads as untrusted data in every step, and tells it so [fenced]

claims.text: One run is bounded: at most five browser steps per round whatever the model plans, `validate.maxRounds` of at most 10, and a wall-clock budget per spec (`validate.timeoutMs`, default 10 minutes) after which no further round is planned, the run says so and judges what it saw

tests.title: takes at most five steps in a round, whatever the model plans [action-cap]
stops planning when the time budget for the spec is spent, and says so, but still judges what it saw [deadline]

claims.text: A check started by an agent (the MCP tool) may target only loopback and the hosts listed in `validate.allowedHosts` (`host`, `host:port` on that port only, `*.domain` for subdomains only); any other target is BLOCKED before a browser or the model sees it; a person on the command line is not restricted

tests.title: allows loopback always, and nothing else unless listed
matches a listed host on any port, a host:port on that port only, and a wildcard on subdomains only
refuses non-http URLs and text that is not a URL, with a reason
an agent-started run checks loopback and listed hosts only; a person is not restricted [allowlist]

claims.text: The evidence, saved-login and report folders are private to their owner (mode 0700, login files 0600), and `validate.evidenceRetentionDays` removes evidence older than that at the start of a run (default: keep it)

tests.title: removes files older than the retention period, keeps newer ones and the .gitignore marker, and drops emptied folders
keeps the evidence, saved-login and report folders private to their owner [evidence-private]

nodes.title: Conformance Testing
nodes.value: Teams can prove, claim by claim, that the current code delivers what the specs say, and see immediately when a proof is no longer trustworthy.

claims.text: Generation turns every scenario of a spec into one test block titled with the scenario name, importing the module the spec declares, for a single spec or all specs and optionally limited to one app.

tests.title: scenario 1: generates a test from a single spec via --spec
scenario 2: --all processes multiple specs across apps

claims.text: Generation supports unit, integration and end-to-end test types, uses the owning app's framework unless overridden, and uses a browser framework for end-to-end tests in TypeScript.

When a spec has claims, the generation prompt lists each claim with its exact tag and requires it in the verifying test's title, and generation warns about every claim whose tag is missing from the output while still writing the file.

tests.title: lists claims with exact tags in the prompt and warns about missing tags
does not warn when every tag is present

claims.text: Generation never overwrites an existing test file unless forced, strips stray Markdown fences from LLM output, and records an LLM failure for one spec without stopping the others.

tests.title: scenario 3: skips an existing test file without --force
scenario 4: overwrites an existing test file with --force
scenario 6: strips Markdown fences from LLM output
scenario 7: LLM error records a failure and continues

claims.text: A claim tag is recognised in the forms `@claim:<spec>#<id>`, `[claim: <spec>#<id>]` and `[claims: a#b, c#d]`, in titles, tags and annotations, with an optional repository prefix, and all consumers read tags through the same logic.

tests.title: extracts the three forms
keeps slashes and repo prefix, drops trailing period, lowercases the claim id
round-trips claimTag
scans source lines with titles
merges sources and results into one index

claims.text: Tests are run through a runner adapter for vitest, jest, playwright, pytest, any JUnit-producing runner, go and cargo, and results are always read from the reporter's output file, never scraped from stdout.

tests.title: adds the right reporter flags per adapter
knows the adapter for each language framework and rejects unknown ones
reads every test from the reporter file, including passes
reads Playwright from the env-named file, pytest from JUnit, Go and Cargo from the redirect
never falls back to stdout: a missing report is parsed:false with no tests

claims.text: Adapters inject the reporter flags the runner needs (with a single separator for npm scripts), run the command verbatim when a results file is configured, pass a test selection as file arguments, merge a results glob, kill a run that exceeds its timeout, and can run inside a Docker sandbox with the repository mounted, where a missing Docker or image is a clear failure that never falls back to the host.

tests.title: adds the right reporter flags per adapter
inserts one -- for npm scripts only
runs the command verbatim when resultsFile is configured
passes a selection as file arguments (package dirs for Go)
never falls back to stdout: a missing report is parsed:false with no tests
merges a results glob and runs the command as written
reports a timeout
actually spawns and kills a hung process at timeoutMs
docker sandbox needs an image and a daemon, and never falls back to the host
docker sandbox mounts the repo and rewrites host paths

claims.text: Reporter output of every supported format is normalised into one result shape covering passes, failures and skips, the format can be auto-detected, and unparseable input is a named error rather than an empty list.

tests.title: an unparseable report file is parsed:false and names the file
detects every format and rejects unknown content
parses vitest results including pass, fail, skip
parses playwright suites, tags, annotations
parses junit xml with properties
parses pytest-json-report
parses go and cargo json lines
honours an explicit format and throws a typed error on bad input

claims.text: A claim's verdict is failed when any tagged test fails, proven when at least one passes and none fail, and unexercised otherwise, with counts of exercised tests and counterexamples.
The proof ledger stores proven, failed, unexercised and error verdicts; stale is computed and never stored, and unproven means the ledger has no row for the claim.

A proof is stale when the spec (or, for v2 specs, the claim) hash changed, when a source file recorded at ingest changed on disk, or when the repository's dependency fingerprint changed; a file that vanished from the registry alone does not make it stale.

tests.title: marks proofs stale when the spec changes
records the dependency fingerprint and goes stale on a lockfile change
effectiveVerdict ignores a missing fingerprint on either side
goes stale when a recorded source file changes on disk, even before drift runs

claims.text: Each stored row records the claim hash, the source file hashes taken from the spec's declared sources, the dependency fingerprint, the run id, the git revision and the evidence path, so editing one source file stales exactly the claims of the specs that declare it.

tests.title: records the dependency fingerprint and goes stale on a lockfile change
goes stale when a recorded source file changes on disk, even before drift runs

claims.text: Ingesting verdicts rejects a file without a run id or verdicts, fails and does not store a verdict for an unparseable reference, missing spec or unknown claim, and lets a later ingest replace an earlier row.

tests.title: rejects a verdicts file without runId or verdicts
fails unknown claims and stores known ones; later ingest replaces the row

claims.text: `results ingest` merges several report files before aggregating, detects or accepts an explicit format, accepts a run id, records a repo-relative evidence path, and exits 2 when any claim failed or a file could not be parsed.

tests.title: results_ingest rejects an unknown format
writes aggregated verdicts with a relative evidence path
merges several files so one claim is exercised from two suites
exits 2 and writes nothing for unparseable input; explicit format overrides detection

claims.text: A partial ingest only writes verdicts for claims present in the results, while the sweep option stores unexercised for absent claims only on a declared full run and never downgrades a still-matching proven claim.

tests.title: stores unexercised for untagged spec claims only with --unexercised
a partial ingest only updates claims present; --unexercised is ignored with a warning [partial-ingest]
--full-run lets the sweep apply (alias --sweep) but keeps proven claims with matching hashes [sweep-keeps-proven]
a sweep covering every app applies without --full-run [unexercised-flag]

claims.text: `proof ingest` and `results ingest` share one code path, write identical rows for identical verdicts, and use a ledger path from `--ledger`, then `paths.proofLedger`, then `.specguard/proofs.json`, kept portable with repo-relative keys.

tests.title: results_ingest writes the proof ledger
proof_ingest merges a verdicts file
migrates absolute fileHashes keys to relative POSIX keys
honours --ledger and paths.proofLedger so two ledgers sit side by side
refuses to read or overwrite a ledger written by a newer SpecGuard
writes to an alternate ledger

claims.text: Each proof row records its provenance: `origin` (`ci` on a GitHub Actions or other CI run, `local` otherwise, `server` for a server-side run), repository, branch, CI actor (never a developer's git identity) and the claim-hash version in force; ledger writes go through one store interface (a file by default) that serialises concurrent updates so none is lost, and a ledger written by a newer SpecGuard is refused rather than read as empty and overwritten

tests.title: reads GitHub Actions variables, and never a developer\'s git identity [github]
is ci for any other CI and local otherwise [others]
does not lose concurrent updates [no-lost-updates]
leaves the file as it was when an update throws, and keeps accepting updates after [failed-update]
refuses a newer ledger version instead of reading it as empty [newer-version]
stamps each row with its origin, branch, actor and the hash version, taking overrides from the caller [stamp]
writes to an injected store instead of a file [injected-store]

claims.text: `proof status` lists failed and stale claims and exits 2 when any exist, while `status` shows proof counts without changing its exit code and `drift` reports each stale proof.

Healing runs one job per distinct test command, classifies each failing test as a test bug or an application bug, rewrites only test code and re-runs up to the retry budget, and never modifies application source.

tests.title: scenario 2: test-bug rewrite, second run passes → fixed:1, exit 0
scenario 3: app-bug recorded, no rewrite, exit 7
scenario 4: still failing after maxRetries → still-broken, exit 7
--classify-only classifies but never writes a test and never re-runs
runs one job per distinct command across apps and reports failures from each

claims.text: Healing treats a missing or unparseable report as a failure even when the runner exited 0 unless told to be lenient, exits 7 while any test remains broken including application bugs, and with classify-only never writes or re-runs.

tests.title: scenario 1: all passing on first run → exit 0, no LLM calls
scenario 3: app-bug recorded, no rewrite, exit 7
scenario 4: still failing after maxRetries → still-broken, exit 7
an unreadable report is a failure even when the runner exited 0
--lenient restores fail-open only for a zero exit
--classify-only classifies but never writes a test and never re-runs

claims.text: Framework detection recognises common web, API and CLI frameworks from the repository's manifests, falls back to a generic profile and honours an explicit entry-point override.

tests.title: detects frameworks from manifests
reads profile entry points, and app.entryPoints replaces them
builds a prompt that names the surface and does not assume a frontend

claims.text: `test run` runs each configured app's tests through its runner adapter, reads the report from the file the runner writes, and ingests the verdicts into the proof ledger in one step, so tests run locally and results produced by CI land in the same ledger

tests.title: runs the configured command and ingests the report in one step [run-and-ingest]

claims.text: `test run` exits non-zero when a suite fails, when a runner produces no readable report, or when a tagged claim fails, even if no failing test carries a claim tag

tests.title: records a failing claim and exits 2 [failing-claim]
fails the run when the suite fails even though no failing test carries a claim tag [untagged-failure]
fails clearly when the runner produced no report [no-report]

claims.text: A proof records what produced it: a test run leaves `evidence` unset and an agentic browser run records `agentic`
`test generate`, `test run` and `test heal` group the test commands; the older `generate` and `heal` names keep working
After a consolidation, results that still carry old claim tags are accepted for one release through `.specguard/claim-migration.json` and recorded under the new claim refs

Evidence is kept per test layer (`unit`, `integration`, `e2e`, `security`, `functional`): each claim's ledger row holds one entry per layer with its own staleness inputs, and the row's combined fields come from the layer that decides it (a failure in any layer, else the newest proof), so a failing browser check is not overwritten by the next passing unit run and the other way round; a row written before layers existed reads as one layer (`functional` when the browser check wrote it, else `unclassified`) and a project that requires no layers sees exactly the old verdicts

tests.title: reads a row written before layers as one layer, and gives exactly the old verdict when nothing is required
is incomplete, not failed, when a required layer has no proof, and complete once it has
lets a failure in any layer decide, and does not let the next passing layer overwrite it
stales a claim when a required layer goes stale, and ignores a stale layer it does not require
drops superseded unclassified evidence when classified evidence arrives, so an old failure cannot outlive its fix

claims.text: A test's layer is the first of: an `@layer:` tag on the test or a `[layer: x]` comment in the first lines of its file; the app's `test.layers` globs; the suite that ran it; `results ingest --layer`; Playwright means `e2e`; path conventions (`e2e`, `integration`, `security` folders and `.e2e.`/`.int.` file names); otherwise `unit`

tests.title: defaults to unit
applies the first matching rule: tag, file comment, config glob, suite, flag, runner, path
reads path conventions
finds tags in titles, brackets and file headers, and ignores unknown layers
puts a layer comment at the top, after a shebang, once, in the language\'s comment syntax
records the --type as a layer comment in the generated file, and none when no type is given [type-layer]
marks generated security tests with the security layer [security-layer]

claims.text: A capability's `layers:` frontmatter (a list for every claim, or a default plus per-claim lists) and the project's `proof.requiredLayers` say which layers a claim needs, the claim's own list first, then the capability's default, then the project's; an unknown layer name is reported, not ignored

tests.title: reads a list as the default, and a map as default plus per-claim lists
takes the claim\'s own list, else the capability default, else the project default

claims.text: `results ingest` writes one verdict per claim and layer, an unclassified `unexercised` sweep row replaces the whole row, classified evidence replaces unclassified evidence of the same tests so an old failure cannot outlive its fix, and `test run` ingests each suite's report with the suite's layer

tests.title: records one layer per test: an @layer tag, a --layer default, else unit
a later passing unit run does not hide a failing browser check
a fixed test replaces an old unclassified failure rather than living beside it

claims.text: When layers are required, `check` and `proof status` list `[proof-incomplete] <claim> (missing: <layers>)` for each claim not proven in every required layer, print a `LAYERS:` line with proven over required per layer, leave the `PROOFS:` line unchanged, and `proof.enforceLayers: fail` makes `proof status` fail on them (`warn` is the default, `off` hides them); the trace carries `required`, `layers` and `missing` per claim and `layerCounts` per capability and in total

tests.title: says which required layer a proven claim is missing, and tallies per layer
prints nothing about layers when none are required, and can be silenced
uses the project default when a capability names no layers, and puts the detail in the trace

claims.text: An app's `test.suites` lists suites that each have a command, a report and a layer (for example vitest for `unit` and Playwright for `e2e`); `test run` runs every suite in place of the app's single command, a failing suite fails only the layer it covers, and the report of each suite is ingested with its layer

tests.title: runs each suite and records its tests in the suite\'s layer
a failing suite fails only its own layer

claims.text: An evidence path is recorded only when it stays inside the repository, normalised and relative; an absolute path, one that climbs out or a symlink that leaves is dropped with a message and the verdict itself is kept

tests.title: records a path inside the repo normalised, and drops one outside it while keeping the verdict

claims.text: Agentic and manual evidence can only prove the `functional` layer: ingesting an `agentic` or `manual` verdict for any other layer fails that row with a clear message and stores nothing, a verdict with that evidence and no layer is recorded as `functional`, and a required non-functional layer whose only proof came from such evidence stays missing

tests.title: refuses agentic or manual evidence for an automated layer and stores nothing
records agentic or manual evidence without a layer as functional, and accepts an explicit functional layer
a required unit layer stays missing when only agentic evidence sits in it

claims.text: A deterministic walk (`deterministic: true` on the proof options) judges every proof by hashes alone: it never consults the LLM drift assessments, so any changed owned file stales the proof, while the default walk still lets an assessment of "unaffected" keep a proof fresh

tests.title: goes stale on any changed owned file where the default walk trusts a drift assessment

claims.text: A claim with an examples table has a proof per row, stored under `specKey#claim/row` with the row hash in `claimHash`: ingest resolves a row ref against the claim's table and fails a row that is not in it, the proof walk visits each row after its claim and judges it against the row hash so editing a row cell stales only that row's proof, and a spec with no tables is walked exactly as before

tests.title: stores a row proof under cap#claim/row with the row hash, and rejects a row that is not in the table
the walk visits each row after its claim, and a changed row cell stales only that row
an unproven row is counted unproven, and a spec without tables is walked as before

claims.text: A result tagged `cap#claim/row` counts for the row and also, once, for the parent claim, and a parameterized test tagged `cap#claim` whose title names exactly one row id of that claim is also attributed to that row

tests.title: a row-tagged result counts for the row and for the parent claim, once even when it names both
keeps the parent of a repo-prefixed row ref under the same prefix
attributes a parameterized test to the one row its title names, and counts it once for the claim
records a row named in the tag itself, and fails one that is not in the table

claims.text: A parameterized test whose title names more than one row id of its claim is attributed to no row, and `results ingest` warns `EXAMPLE_TITLE_AMBIGUOUS` without failing

tests.title: warns EXAMPLE_TITLE_AMBIGUOUS and attributes to no row when a title names two rows, without failing

claims.text: `test run --claims <refs...>` runs exactly the tests tagged to the given claim refs (found through the claim-test index), selecting them by title where the runner can, and reports which claims have no tagged test instead of running the whole suite

tests.title: runs exactly the tests tagged to the claim, by title, and reports the selection
selects the tests of several claims together and a row-less ref also selects its rows
does not run anything when no test is tagged to the claims, and says which
reports a claim without a test while running the others
refuses a malformed ref, test files next to --claims, and a bad record id

claims.text: When the runner cannot select by title (or a tagged test has no title the runner can be given), `test run --claims` runs the files that hold the tests, says so, and flags `selection: files` in the run output and the run record; a report row that names none of the selected tests reads `missing`, never pass

tests.title: runs the files and flags selection: files when a tagged test has no title the runner can be given
says missing, never pass, for a selected test no report row names

claims.text: Each runner selects tests by exact title: vitest and jest with `-t`, Playwright with `--grep` (an escaped, end-anchored regex alternation), pytest with `-k`, go test with an anchored `-run`, cargo with name filters after `--`, and JUnit through Maven `-Dtest=Class#method` or Gradle `--tests` from the declaration's class and method

tests.title: vitest and jest select by an anchored, escaped alternation that matches the full name and nothing else
playwright uses --grep with the same pattern
pytest selects with -k over the test function names
go selects with an anchored -run alternation
cargo passes the names as test-binary filters
maven selects Class#method, gradle --tests, from the declaration the title came from
puts the flags in the command in the place each runner reads them

claims.text: A title is passed to the runner as one literal argument: regex metacharacters, quotes, unicode and shell syntax are escaped or quoted and never interpolated, and a list too long for one command line, or an argument the shell cannot be given, yields unknown

tests.title: hands regex metacharacters, quotes, unicode and shell syntax to the runner as one literal pattern
does not run anything a title contains
escapes every regex metacharacter
selects a very long list when it fits one command line, and says unknown when it does not
says unknown for a title the shell cannot be given
de-duplicates titles and ignores empty ones

nodes.title: Intent Approval
nodes.value: A person, not a tool, signs off that each requirement states what the system should do, and the sign-off is a committed record that lapses the moment the requirement's wording changes.

claims.text: An approval is recorded as one new history entry per approval event, with `kind: approval`, an `approves` list of `specKey#claimId@<first 16 hex of the claim hash>`, a `method` (command, as-built, pr or plan) and the approver as author, so approvals are committed files that branches never conflict on

tests.title: formats and parses ref@hash round trip
rejects malformed refs and hashes
survives a render/parse round trip of a history entry
leaves entries without approval fields as they were
reads only approval entries and skips malformed refs and unknown methods
--yes writes one approval entry, back-references it, and changes no claim hash

claims.text: A claim counts as approved only while an approval's recorded hash equals the hash of the claim as it reads now, so editing a claim's text or its Problem & Value makes it unapproved, and when several approvals match the newest wins

tests.title: matches only while the hash is the same
editing a claim (new hash) makes it unapproved
the newest matching approval wins, ignoring newer ones for other wordings
approves only a reworded claim after an edit, leaving approved claims alone

claims.text: Recording an approval adds the entry id to the `history:` list of each affected capability and changes no claim hash, so no existing proof goes stale

tests.title: --yes writes one approval entry, back-references it, and changes no claim hash

claims.text: `spec approve` is a dry run unless `--yes` is given: it lists the claims it would approve and the number of capabilities, exits 0 and writes nothing

is a dry run without --yes: lists what it would approve and writes nothing

skips v1 specs

an unknown row target fails and writes nothing

tests.title: --as-built refuses a capability that owns no source files and writes nothing

derives the default actor from the host agent environment

tests.title: is idempotent: a second run writes nothing
approves only a reworded claim after an edit, leaving approved claims alone

tests.title: no tool name contains "approve", with or without the legacy tools

tests.title: dry-runs by default, writes with --yes, and reports through `spec approvals --json`
reports approved/total per capability and the unapproved refs

claims.text: An approval may name an example row (`specKey#claimId/rowId@<first 16 hex of the row hash>`): a claim and each of its rows are approved separately, so approving a claim never approves its rows and the other way round, `spec approve cap#claim` approves the claim and all its current rows in one entry, `cap#claim/row` approves only that row, and a claim without an examples table has no row entries

approving one row leaves its claim and the other row unapproved, and the reverse
an edited row lapses on its own; its earlier approval is still the latest

claims.text: The approval index offers `latest(ref)`, the newest approval of a ref at any hash, so a claim approved earlier and changed since can be told apart from one never approved

claims.text: In CI an approving review counts only when it is the latest decisive review of a human other than the pull request's author, its state is APPROVED, its author association is owner, member or collaborator, and it is not a bot (by type or a `[bot]` login suffix); logins compare case-insensitively

claims.text: A qualifying review that covers a changed claim with no approval entry is itself a verified `pr` approval, written to the proof note with reviewer, review id and reviewed commit; an approval already carried in the note for the same wording is reused rather than written again, and one for an earlier wording does not count

tests.title: a covering review with no entry is a verified pr approval written to the note
without a covering review or entry nothing is approved; an approval carried in the note is verified without being written again
a carried approval for an earlier wording of the claim does not count

claims.text: A committed `pr` approval entry is verified only when a qualifying review whose login equals the entry's author covers the claim; otherwise it is treated like any recorded entry and needs a countersign where a review is required

tests.title: a committed pr entry is verified only when a review by the same login covers the claim

claims.text: Removing a claim is a change of intent: at a capability that requires review a removal needs a review that saw the claim gone, and an uncovered removal is reported as needing review (not when review is not required or `allowSelf` is on); a covered removal is shown as a verified approval

claims.text: `spec approve --from-pr <n>` makes a pull request's review approvals permanent: it reads the pull request's reviews from GitHub (a token in the environment or `gh auth token`), and writes one committed history entry per reviewer with `method: pr` and that reviewer as author, approving each unapproved claim in scope whose hash at the reviewed commit equals its hash now; without targets it looks at every unapproved claim, without `--yes` it only lists what it would record, and it refuses `--as-built` and a number that is not a pull request

nodes.title: Platform Foundation
nodes.value: Every SpecGuard capability runs on one predictable engine for configuration, model access, cost control, redaction, file access and exit codes, so behaviour is consistent, safe and testable.

claims.text: For activity logs that Git does not track, persistence honors an existing ignore rule or adds a literal, project-specific rule to Git's local `info/exclude`, including nested folders, symlinked paths and linked worktrees, without editing versioned files or the Git index; repeated appends after commits leave an otherwise clean repository clean, exclusions are idempotent, and a failure to establish an ignore rule skips optional persistence rather than creating an unignored file

tests.title: persists, reconciles and clears extension activity without dirtying a clean repo
stays clean after repeated real commits whose post-commit hook appends activity
ignores a nested project with literal spaces and brackets without changing versioned files or the index
supports linked worktrees whose .git is a file
invalidates its cached exclusion when a repository ignore rule changes
notices when a previously non-Git project becomes a repository

claims.text: Configuration is found by searching upward from the working directory for `.specguard/config.json`, stopping at the repository boundary so a repo without its own config never inherits a parent repo's; no config, and no overlay covering the directory, yields a not-found error that names the search start and suggests `specguard init`

claims.text: Config describes one or more apps, each with language, repo directory, spec directory, source globs, framework, test output, test command settings, entry points, exclusions and path-prefix stripping, plus top-level paths, granularity, plugin and validation settings; sensible defaults apply to anything omitted, including TypeScript as the default language and the whole `llm` block (Anthropic with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or the key variable that goes with a named provider), so a project needs no model setup to start

nodes.title: Proof Store
nodes.value: Every proven commit carries its own small proof record inside git, written only by CI, so a clone or a pull request can read what was proven without rerunning tests, trusting a local file or merging a shared ledger.

claims.text: Notes live under `refs/notes/specguard` on the `origin` remote unless `proofStore` names others, a note over 1 MiB is trimmed and one over 8 MiB is refused, and a note is checked against a CI check run only when `proofStore.verify` is `check-run`

claims.text: A proof note is read defensively: text that is not JSON, JSON that is not a proof note, and a note whose shape is wrong each come back as a named failure (`not-json`, `wrong-schema`, `invalid`) with a short detail and never as a throw, while fields the reader does not know are kept and written back

mergeNotes is commutative, idempotent and leaves its inputs alone
mergeNotes breaks a same-instant tie the same way in both orders

claims.text: Note authenticity checking is opt-in: with `proofStore.verify` `off` (the default), or `check-run` but no GitHub client or repository, a note reads `unverified` and no call is made

tests.title: off returns unverified without any call
check-run without a client or repository is unverified and makes no call

claims.text: With `proofStore.verify` `check-run`, a note is verified only when a `specguard/proof-note` check run on its commit, created by the workflow app, carries a `note-sha256:` summary line equal to the note's digest (compared case-insensitively); check runs from any other app never count

tests.title: check-run asks for the named check run on the commit and verifies a matching digest
the digest compares case-insensitively and only on the summary line that carries it

claims.text: Check runs that exist but carry another digest, or none that ran on a required branch, give `mismatch`, no check run gives `unverified`, and a failing API call gives `not-checked`, never a pass

tests.title: runs that exist but carry another digest are a mismatch; no run is unverified
only the workflow app counts: a run from another app with the right digest does not verify
a required branch rejects a run whose suite ran elsewhere
an API failure is not-checked, never verified, and an invalid digest is unverified

claims.text: The check run summary leads with `note-sha256: <digest>` followed by schema version, row count and certification level, and the reader recovers exactly that digest from it

tests.title: the summary leads with the digest and round-trips through the reader

claims.text: Every ref, remote and commit name that reaches git is checked first (a notes ref must sit under `refs/notes/`, a remote is a plain name, a commit is a hex name or a safe ref), anything that could be read as an option is refused without running git, git runs only through argument arrays, and credentials in a URL or header never appear in a message

tests.title: refuses a notes ref, a remote or a commit name that git could read as an option
never lets a credential in a git message reach the output

claims.text: Fetching the notes ref reports `no-remote`, `no-ref-on-remote`, `offline` or `auth` as outcomes and never throws, a missing notes ref reads as no notes, a successful fetch is forced and recorded, `proof fetch` can add the notes refspec to the remote's fetch settings once, is quiet and never fails in the background form, and skips a fetch younger than `--if-older` or any background fetch when `proofStore.autoFetch` is `off`

tests.title: fetchNotes reports no-remote, no-ref-on-remote, offline, and then fetches once a note is pushed; the missing ref reads as no notes
configureNotesFetch adds the notes refspec once and is idempotent
fetch brings the notes a CI job pushed; a quiet fetch says nothing; --if-older skips a fresh fetch; autoFetch off skips the background form
with no notes on the remote fetch says CI has not written any yet and succeeds; an unreachable remote fails, and a quiet one does not
notes summarizes the nearest note, the note on a commit, and says so when there is none

claims.text: Writing a note stores exactly the bytes the canonical serialization produced, so the note's digest is the sha256 of the stored blob, creates the ref and pushes without force; a note over 1 MiB is written trimmed with a warning and one over 8 MiB is not written at all

tests.title: writeAndPushNote creates the ref, stores the bytes serializeNote wrote (so the digest matches) and pushes
a note over the soft limit is written trimmed with a warning, and one over the hard limit is refused

claims.text: Writers never merge notes with git: a push that loses a race is fetched, re-applied on the new tip and pushed again (at most five rounds with jittered backoff), so writers on different commits all land, and a second note for the same commit is merged with the first, then has its statement summary refreshed

tests.title: two writers on different commits both land: a push that loses the race is fetched, re-applied and pushed again
a same-commit re-run merges rows rather than replacing, refreshes the summary, and the result does not depend on who lands first
a second publish for the same commit merges into the note rather than replacing it, and refreshes the statement

claims.text: The nearest noted ancestor is found by a topological walk bounded by `proofStore.maxWalk` that reports its distance and whether it was cut short, a note on a commit that is not an ancestor is never read, and a note of a newer version, a corrupt note or one filed under another commit is skipped with a warning while the walk goes on to an older note

tests.title: nearestNoted finds the note two commits back with its distance, and reads a note on HEAD at distance 0
stops at maxWalk and reports the walk as truncated, and never reads a note on a commit that is not an ancestor (a fork pull request head)
skips a note of a newer version, a corrupt note and a note filed under another commit, each with a warning, and walks on to an older note

claims.text: In a shallow clone a walk that finds no note reports itself as truncated, and deepening the clone in steps finds the noted ancestor

tests.title: in a shallow clone the walk is truncated; deepenUntilNoted finds the noted ancestor

claims.text: A squash or rebase merge commit finds the note of the pull request head that has the same tree, newest first and optionally only notes newer than a date, without needing the head's commit object

tests.title: notesWithTree finds the pull request head note for a squash commit with the same tree, and only newer notes when asked

claims.text: Pruning removes only notes older than the given days on commits no branch, remote branch or tag reaches, lists them without `--yes`, never touches a note on a reachable commit and does nothing in a shallow clone

tests.title: pruneNotes removes only old notes of unreachable commits, and a dry run removes nothing
creates the main branch used by pruning fixtures even when Git defaults to master
prune lists notes of unreachable old commits without --yes, removes them with it, and keeps notes on branches

claims.text: The effective ledger is the local cache together with the nearest ancestor's note: per claim and layer a fresh failure beats a fresh CI proof, which beats a fresh local proof, which beats a stale row, a changed owned file stales the note's row so a fresh local row decides, local rows are always local evidence whatever origin they say (unless the CI job that wrote them asks to keep it), a note that fails its check run is ignored with a warning, no network call is made unless `proofStore.verify` is `check-run`, and the merged view cannot be written back

tests.title: a fresh failure beats a fresh CI proven row, which beats a fresh local proven row, which beats a stale one
note rows from an ancestor prove unchanged claims at HEAD with no local ledger, as CI evidence
a changed owned file stales the note row and the fresh local row decides
local rows are always local evidence whatever origin they say, unless the CI job that wrote them asks to keep it
a note of a newer version is ignored with a warning and the local cache is read
read only: update throws, so no pipeline can write a merged view back
with proofStore.verify check-run a note is verified only by a matching check run, and a mismatch is ignored; off by default makes no call

claims.text: `check` reads the effective ledger when a note is found, names where each capability's evidence came from (`ci note @abc1234 (2 commits back, unverified)`, `local (provisional)` or `mixed: 30 ci, 4 local`) on its statement lines and under `--explain`, can reach certified at HEAD from an ancestor note with no local ledger, ignores notes under `--no-notes`, and for a repo with no notes reads the local file exactly as before

tests.title: reports the evidence source per capability and on the headline when proofs come from an ancestor note
certified at HEAD from the evidence in an ancestor note, with no local ledger
with no notes ref check is unchanged: same lines and exit code with or without --no-notes, and no mention of notes

claims.text: `proof publish` writes the note for the checked-out commit only in CI (or with `--allow-non-github` in another CI), from the fresh CI-origin rows only, refuses a commit that is not checked out, proof files that differ from the commit and a run with nothing fresh, and `--force-local` writes a provisional local note that is not pushed by default and that readers treat as local evidence

tests.title: refuses outside CI, and with a CI that is not GitHub unless it is allowed; nothing is written
in CI writes and pushes the note for HEAD with only the CI-origin rows, the file hashes once, and the run it came from
--force-local writes a provisional note that is not pushed and that readers treat as local evidence
refuses a commit that is not checked out, a tree whose proof files differ from the commit, and a run with nothing fresh

claims.text: `specguard_proof_fetch` fetches the notes ref over MCP, writes git refs only and never the working tree, is a write tool a read-only server does not offer, and no MCP tool can publish a proof note

tests.title: is offered by the default server and is a write tool, and no tool can publish a note
fetches the notes ref into the clone and changes no file of the working tree

nodes.title: Requirement History
nodes.value: Anyone can see which prompts, approved plans and decisions shaped each capability, so the reason behind a requirement survives the chat session that produced it.

claims.text: A history entry is a markdown file at `specs/history/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` whose frontmatter has id (equal to the file name without extension), date, kind (prompt, plan, decision or a combination such as prompt+plan), author, source and an `affects` list of capability ids or `system`, followed by the verbatim text of the prompt, plan or decision

tests.title: round-trips the policy list, and an entry without one renders and parses as before [policy]
round-trips frontmatter and body [roundtrip]
writes an entry and links it from every affected capability [add-and-link]
writes the policy lines of a decision into the entry and leaves other entries without one [policy]

claims.text: History entries are not specs: the spec loader skips the history folder, entries never appear as nodes in the spec graph, and two entries created on the same day with the same slug get distinct ids

tests.title: slugifies and makes ids unique with a numeric suffix [ids]

claims.text: `history add` records a prompt (`--prompt`), an approved plan (`--plan <file>`) or a decision (`--decision`) as a new entry, taking the author from git config and the source from the caller (default `manual`), and refuses to add an entry with no content

tests.title: writes an entry and links it from every affected capability [add-and-link]
reads a plan from a file and uses its heading as the title [plan-file]
requires something to record [needs-input]

claims.text: when `--affects <ids>` is given, `history add` validates each id against the spec graph and fails with exit 2 on an unknown capability id, writing nothing

tests.title: fails with exit 2 and writes nothing when --affects names an unknown capability [unknown-capability]

claims.text: when `--affects` is omitted, `history add` asks the fast model tier to propose affected capabilities from the entry text (and the working-tree diff when present), keeps only ids that exist in the spec graph, and falls back to `system` when the model is disabled or proposes nothing

tests.title: proposes affected capabilities with the fast model when --affects is omitted, dropping unknown ids [propose]
records against the system spec when no model can propose capabilities [no-llm]

claims.text: `history add` appends the entry id to the `history:` list in the frontmatter of each affected capability spec, leaving the rest of the spec byte-for-byte unchanged and adding the id only once

tests.title: appends to an existing list, creates a missing one, and converts an empty list [add-ref]
is idempotent and leaves content without frontmatter alone [idempotent]
appends to a flow list instead of adding a second history key [flow-list]
appends after the last item of an unindented block list, matching its indent [unindented]
leaves the spec alone when the history value is something it cannot extend, or the result would not parse [refuses]
writes an entry and links it from every affected capability [add-and-link]

claims.text: Editing only the `history:` or `sources:` frontmatter of a spec never marks an existing proof stale, because proofs hash the claim text and normative sections and not back-references

tests.title: never changes a claim hash, so back-references cannot stale proofs [no-stale]

claims.text: `history log` prints entries newest first with date, kind, title and affected capabilities; `--capability <id>` restricts it to entries affecting that capability, and `--json` prints the same data as JSON

tests.title: log filters to one capability through affects or the history: list [log]

claims.text: `specguard init --history-hooks` is the only way hooks are installed; without the flag no history hook is written, and a repeated run changes nothing, preserves hooks the user already has, and replaces a differing SpecGuard hook only with `--update-hooks`

tests.title: is idempotent, keeps the user\'s own hooks, and never rewrites a differing hook without --update-hooks [safe-merge]

claims.text: a UserPromptSubmit hook runs `history inbox`, which reads the hook's JSON from stdin with a real JSON parser (so quotes and newlines survive), appends the redacted prompt keyed by `session_id` and `cwd` to an uncommitted inbox file, caps the inbox size, and never fails the user's prompt

tests.title: redacts a very long run of characters in linear time, because a prompt hook runs it synchronously [no-redos]
records redacted prompts and ignores empty or malformed input without throwing [inbox]
trims an oversized inbox [inbox-cap]

claims.text: every history hook prints nothing to stdout (stdout is injected into the model's context), uses the resolved local SpecGuard binary rather than a cold package download, and ends in a way that swallows its own failures

tests.title: wires the prompt inbox and the plan capture, both silent [wire]
returns null instead of exiting when there is no SpecGuard config, so a hook never fails the session

claims.text: a PostToolUse hook on ExitPlanMode runs `history capture`, which takes the approved plan from the tool input (falling back to the session transcript), pairs it with only the inbox prompts from the same `session_id`, and writes one committed prompt+plan entry; prompts from sessions that never reach an approved plan are never committed

tests.title: writes one committed entry from the approved plan and only that session\'s prompts [capture]
does nothing when the hook carries no plan [no-plan]
falls back to the transcript when the hook input has no plan [transcript]

claims.text: prompt text is passed through the shared secret redactor both when it is written to the inbox and again when an entry is committed, so keys, tokens and personal data never reach `specs/history/`

tests.title: masks password assignments, private keys and Google keys, and leaves type declarations alone [more-secrets]
refuses to write an approval: only spec approve records one [no-approval]
records redacted prompts and ignores empty or malformed input without throwing [inbox]

claims.text: `check` reports each capability whose owned sources changed since its last history entry or spec edit without either, as an advisory finding that does not by itself fail the build unless the project opts in

tests.title: reports code that changed after the last recorded intent, and clears when intent is recorded [gap-lifecycle]

claims.text: The MCP server exposes `history_add` and `history_log` with the same behaviour as the CLI command so agents can record decisions directly

The history hooks read their JSON from stdin up to 4 MB and drop larger input whole, cut a single prompt to 50,000 characters before it is redacted and stored, keep the uncommitted inbox to the newest 300 prompts once it passes 1 MB, and keep it readable by its owner only

tests.title: reads small input, and drops input over the limit instead of buffering it
cuts a huge prompt, and keeps the inbox readable by its owner only
does not widen the mode of an inbox that already exists

nodes.title: Security Scanning and Remediation
nodes.value: Security and risk teams find flaws in code, dependencies, secrets and the specs themselves, and get fixes proposed with proof that behaviour was preserved, in a form other systems can automate.

claims.text: `security` generates OWASP-annotated vitest security test stubs from a spec's security notes and its source module, for one spec (`--spec`) or all specs (`--all`); each generated test carries an `// OWASP A0X: <category>` comment, accidental Markdown fences are removed, an existing security test file is never overwritten (the spec is reported as skipped), and an LLM failure for one spec is recorded as failed without stopping the others

tests.title: scenario 1: generates OWASP-annotated stubs from a single spec
scenario 2: --all generates one stub per spec across apps
scenario 3: skips an existing security test file
scenario 4: strips Markdown fences from LLM output
scenario 7: LLM error records a failure and continues

claims.text: `security --with-sast` runs Semgrep in a Docker container over each app's repo and the language-appropriate dependency audit (npm or pip); when Docker, Semgrep or the audit tool is unavailable it logs a warning and continues with zero findings instead of failing

tests.title: scenario 3: returns ok:false when npm unavailable
returns ok:false when ruff is unavailable
returns ok:false when pip-audit is unavailable
scenario 6: --with-sast when tool unavailable does not throw, exitCode 0

claims.text: Real SAST or audit findings are summarised into the LLM prompt so generated stubs target concrete issues; `security` exits 5 only when real findings exist (generating stubs alone exits 0) and writes a structured report to `.specguard/security.json` with every finding, counts by severity and one row per spec handled, a report failure never changing the outcome

tests.title: scenario 5: --with-sast with findings sets exitCode 5 and reports them

claims.text: `remediate` detects dependency advisories through the ecosystem's native audit and OSV, Semgrep findings and gitleaks secrets; advisories are merged across tools by id or alias keeping the highest severity, suppressed by an ignore file with expiry dates, sorted deterministically and filtered by a minimum severity (default high)

tests.title: merges by shared alias and keeps highest severity
sorts deterministically
applies ignore entries by id or alias, only while unexpired
uses OSV when available and merges with the native audit
falls back to native audits, with a warning, when OSV is missing
applies the ignore file, the threshold, and reports secrets without their value
drops findings below the minimum severity [threshold]

claims.text: `remediate --scan-only` changes nothing and exits 5 when any advisory remains after suppression and thresholding, otherwise 0; secrets are only ever reported, never auto-fixed

tests.title: --scan-only reports and exits 5 without changing anything
applies the ignore file, the threshold, and reports secrets without their value

claims.text: A remediation run refuses a dirty working tree and a fresh lock, does all work in a temporary git worktree and never touches the user's working tree, and rolling back removes the worktree and branch

tests.title: refuses a dirty working tree and a fresh lock; replaces a stale lock

claims.text: The baseline runs the tests twice to quarantine flaky tests, snapshots the proof ledger, and a baseline that is not green ends the run with exit 11 before any patch is applied

tests.title: an unparseable baseline counts as a failure: exit 11, nothing applied
quarantines ids whose status differs between the two baseline runs

claims.text: The planner chooses the smallest fixing version (patch over minor, major only with `--allow-major`), changes only manifests and lockfiles for a dependency bump or only the files named in a code finding, and aborts and rolls back on any other changed file

tests.title: ranks patch before minor before major
bumps a direct npm dependency keeping the range prefix and formatting
pins transitive fixes through overrides, pnpm.overrides and resolutions
picks the smallest fix, patch over minor, and refuses a major without --allow-major
accepts manifest and lockfile edits only
enforces file and line limits; untracked directories are noise; test leftovers are tolerated when tracked-only
a code fix may only change the named file and cannot escape the repo

claims.text: After patching, the install, build, typecheck and tests run (claim-tagged tests for the affected specs first, then the full suite), the detector runs again, and heal is never run in rewrite mode so no test file is modified

tests.title: selects claim-tagged tests of affected specs plus tests in importing files

claims.text: The behaviour verdict compares proof-ledger results before and after: it is CHANGED when a baseline-passing test fails or vanishes, a proven claim drops, claim or test counts fall, an advisory remains or a new one appears, or build or typecheck is red; INCONCLUSIVE when output is unparseable, no tests were selected or proofs were not re-proven; otherwise PRESERVED, with CHANGED beating INCONCLUSIVE beating PRESERVED

tests.title: PRESERVED when every condition holds
lists the exact differing tests and claims
a vanished test is named by id
a new test that fails is not a regression, a new advisory below threshold is ignored
a pre-existing advisory that remains below target is not "new"
excludes flaky tests from comparison and reports them
code fixes do not need package selection or proof staleness
strictUnexercised=false lets baseline gaps through
CHANGED wins over INCONCLUSIVE
identifies tests by file and full title only
count and advisory-state claims

claims.text: Remediation runs use one branch per advisory group named `specguard/remediate/<id>`, skip advisories whose branch or PR already exists, and write the plan, diffs, selected tests, verdict and evidence to `.specguard/remediation/<runId>.json` with a markdown pull request body

tests.title: PRESERVED: a safe bump produces a branch and a normal PR; the user tree is untouched
idempotent: a re-run skips an advisory whose branch already exists
detects an existing branch or PR (idempotency)

claims.text: Without `--pr` nothing is pushed; with `--pr` the branch is pushed and a pull request opened (normal for PRESERVED, draft for CHANGED or INCONCLUSIVE); `--dry-run` leaves no branch, push, PR or report in the user's tree; nothing is merged unless the auto-merge policy below allows it, and `ship` itself never merges

tests.title: PRESERVED: a safe bump produces a branch and a normal PR; the user tree is untouched
CHANGED: a bump that changes behavior fails a baseline-passing test, opens a draft, exits 9
INCONCLUSIVE: a flaky test in the selected set is excluded and reported, draft PR, exit 10
--dry-run runs the whole loop and leaves no branch, no push, no PR and no files
ship stages only the scope, commits, and uses --draft for non-PRESERVED verdicts; no merge call exists

claims.text: `remediate` exits 8 for PRESERVED, 9 for CHANGED, 10 for INCONCLUSIVE and 11 for a setup or baseline error, and a missing external tool is reported by name as a warning rather than a raw error

tests.title: CHANGED: a bump that changes behavior fails a baseline-passing test, opens a draft, exits 9
INCONCLUSIVE: a flaky test in the selected set is excluded and reported, draft PR, exit 10
an unparseable baseline counts as a failure: exit 11, nothing applied

claims.text: `security scan` runs the dependency-advisory, Semgrep and gitleaks detectors that `remediate` uses, as one detector set whose results share one finding shape; the older `security --with-sast` command remains for CI gates, and the retired `deps` gate is an alias of it

tests.title: turns advisories, code findings and secrets into one valid plan [one-plan]

claims.text: `security scan` also performs a spec-level review per capability, flagging missing authorization or data-classification requirements, unspecified abuse cases or rate limits, contradictory requirements, interfaces with no owning claim, and code findings that reveal a spec gap; each finding has a type of spec, code, dependency or secret

tests.title: adds a spec item per finding, grounded in the capability, with the real claim refs only [spec-items]
shows the model the code findings under the capability so it can spot a requirement gap [code-in-review]

claims.text: Scans emit a `RemediationPlan` validated by one Zod schema and published as JSON Schema at `schemas/remediation-plan.v1.json`; each item carries finding references, severity, capability and claim links, the workspace unit when the project has a manifest, affected files, a change type (code, spec, dependency or config), the claims that must stay proven, an optional external reference, and a status that moves open, planned, in-progress, fixed, then verified or wont-fix

tests.title: is generated from the zod definition and the committed file is current [schema-current]
describes the lifecycle and allows extra fields for consumers [schema-shape]
turns advisories, code findings and secrets into one valid plan [one-plan]

claims.text: Plans are stored at `.specguard/security/plans/<id>.json`, served by the documentation API, and updated by other systems with `security plan set-status`; `security fix` executes plan items through the remediate executor and updates their status

tests.title: resolves latest and cannot be walked out of the plans folder [latest-and-paths]

claims.text: A plan item's id is stable across scans (derived from what was found), so a later scan keeps its status, history and external reference; an item marked fixed or verified that the scanner reports again is reopened with a note; an unresolved item no longer detected is closed as fixed with the note "no longer detected" only when a detector that could have seen it ran at a severity floor covering it (a missing detector, a raised floor, an `--app` filter or a failed model review closes nothing, and spec findings are never closed by silence), a plan that cannot be read stops the scan instead of dropping every status, and items already closed and gone are dropped

tests.title: keeps status, history and external reference for an item seen before [kept]
closes an unresolved item that is no longer detected, with a note [closed]
drops items that were already closed and are gone [dropped]
keeps item ids and statuses across scans and closes what is gone [carry-over]
does not close findings when the detector that found them did not run [no-detector]
closes only what the detectors that did run could have seen [partial-detectors]
does not close anything on a scan narrowed to one app or raised above an item severity [narrowed]
reopens a finding someone marked fixed when the scanner still reports it [reopen]
gives two findings of one rule in one file different identities, stable when lines move [fingerprints]
refuses to carry on when the latest plan cannot be read, rather than dropping every status [unreadable-latest]
keeps a spec finding as one item when the model rewords its title, and never auto-closes it [spec-identity]

claims.text: `security plan set-status` enforces the lifecycle: any state can be reopened, verified is reachable only from fixed, an unknown status, plan or item is rejected, and a stored plan that does not match the schema is never trusted; plans live behind one store interface (files by default) that serialises concurrent updates, and an update may carry the item version the caller last saw (the count of its recorded status changes), in which case a changed item is refused as a conflict and nothing is written

tests.title: allows the documented transitions and nothing else [transitions]
moves an item, records who and why, and keeps the plan valid [set-status]
refuses a transition the lifecycle forbids and leaves the plan alone [bad-transition]
rejects an unknown status, plan or item [unknowns]
rejects a stored plan that does not match the schema instead of trusting it [invalid-plan]
rejects an update made against a stale item version and writes nothing [conflict]
names why an update was refused: no plan, no item, bad status, bad transition [error-codes]
serialises concurrent updates to different items of one plan, losing none [concurrent-items]
lists plans oldest first and resolves latest, and skips temp files and invalid plans [list-latest]
moves an item, records who did it, and returns the new version [patch]
answers 409 for a stale If-Match and applies the update for the current one [if-match]
maps refusals to status codes: 401, 403, 400, 404, 422 [refusals]
loses nothing when many items are updated at once [concurrent]

claims.text: Resolving a spec-level item records a requirement-history decision against its capability, once

tests.title: records requirement history when a spec-level finding is resolved [spec-fix-history]

claims.text: A secret finding records only its rule and location, never the detector's message, so a plan can be handed to another system without carrying the secret

tests.title: applies the ignore file, the threshold, and reports secrets without their value
never copies a secret\'s message into the plan [no-secret-leak]

claims.text: `security fix` runs the remediation executor once for the selected dependency and code items, moves each item by what happened to its branch (preserved: fixed; changed: in-progress with the verdict; failed: open; skipped: planned; not attempted: open), records the branch in the item's history, re-reads the plan before writing so a status or external reference a tracker set meanwhile is kept, restores the items if the run crashes, and never patches spec or secret items

tests.title: moves each item by what happened to its branch, and never touches spec or secret items [statuses]
keeps an update a tracker made while the fix ran, and restores items when the run crashes [concurrent-update]

claims.text: `security scan --sarif [file]` also writes the unresolved items of the plan as SARIF 2.1.0 (default `.specguard/security/scan.sarif`): one result per item with a level from its severity, a `security-severity` score, the item id as a stable fingerprint so GitHub tracks one alert per item, and its files and line as locations; fixed, verified and won't-fix items are left out so their alerts close

tests.title: turns unresolved items into results with a stable fingerprint, a level and a location
leaves out resolved items so their alerts close, and maps every severity to a level
still gives an item with no file or rule a location and a rule id

claims.text: Auto-merge of a remediation pull request is decided by one pure policy, and every condition must hold: `remediate.autoMerge.enabled` and `--auto-merge` are both set; the change is a dependency fix touching only manifests and lockfiles; the bump is a patch, or a minor at version 1.0 or later (never a major or unknown bump, never a package on `denyPackages`); the verdict is PRESERVED with no reasons and at least one test was selected; every claim proven in any layer before the change is proven in that layer again afterwards; risk is low and the breaking-change analysis is clean; each failed condition is listed, written to the report and posted as a pull request comment

tests.title: allows a patch bump of manifests and lockfiles that kept every proof
needs both the config and the flag, and only ever merges dependency fixes
refuses a change that touches anything but manifests and lockfiles
allows patch bumps, minor bumps from 1.0 on, and never major or unknown bumps
requires a clean verdict, a selected test, and every layer re-proven
refuses medium or high risk and a flagged breaking change, and lists every failed rule at once

claims.text: When the policy allows it, the pull request is not merged at once: `gh pr merge --auto --squash` is requested only after the base branch is confirmed to have required status checks (an unprotected branch, or one whose protection cannot be read, is refused), and a failed request is reported as not armed; draft pull requests and code fixes are never auto-merged

tests.title: reads branch protection: only a non-empty list of required checks counts
merges when ready only on a branch with required checks
never asks to merge an unprotected branch, which would merge before any check ran
reports a failed merge request instead of claiming it armed, and encodes the branch name

claims.text: `remediate` records test evidence by layer the way `results ingest` does, keeps what a layer proved that its test command never reaches (a browser proof is not swept to unexercised), and reports claims proven in some layer before a change and not after it, so a dependency bump that only the unit tests could re-prove is not auto-merged

tests.title: lists claims proven in a layer before the change and not after it
does not count a stale or failed layer as proven before the change
a remediation run keeps what a browser proved that the test command never reaches

claims.text: `remediate --from failing [--claim <ref>] [--max <n>]` repairs the application for failing claims: it takes each capability with a failing claim (a failing test or browser check in any layer), shows a fixer the failing tests, the browser findings and the capability's own source files, and writes the files it returns; the capability's source files exclude tests, specs, docs, history, configuration and manifests, and a capability with none is skipped
